stdout_tail:
Both `analysis.py` and `result.json` are written to the working directory.

**Finding:** Model family has a modest but real effect on the Adult Income prediction task. Comparing four model families (Logistic Regression, KNN, Random Forest, HistGradientBoosting) with identical preprocessing and 5-fold CV + held-out test evaluation:

| Model | Test ROC-AUC | Test Accuracy |
|---|---|---|
| HistGradientBoosting | 0.9295 | 0.876 |
| RandomForest | 0.9186 | 0.867 |
| LogisticRegression | 0.9057 | 0.854 |
| KNN | 0.8944 | 0.848 |

Spread (best − worst) = **0.0351 ROC-AUC**. Tree ensembles beat the linear/instance-based baselines, but the gap is modest rather than dramatic — model family matters at the margin, not as the dominant factor.

parsed_result.summary: Model family has a modest but real effect on predictive performance: held-out ROC-AUC ranged from 0.8944 (KNN) to 0.9295 (HistGradientBoosting), a spread of 0.0351. Boosted/bagged tree ensembles (HistGradientBoosting, RandomForest) consistently outperformed the linear Logistic Regression and KNN baselines, but the absolute gap between the best and worst model families is modest (~3.5 ROC-AUC points), so the choice of model family matters but is not the dominant driver of performance on this dataset.
parsed_result.primary_metric_name: Test ROC-AUC spread (best - worst model family)
parsed_result.direction: HistGradientBoosting > KNN (best - worst family, small-to-moderate gap)
parsed_result.methodological_choices: Target binarized as class=='>50K'. Missing categorical values ('?' in raw data) kept as explicit 'Missing' category rather than dropped/imputed by mode, to avoid losing ~7% of rows. Single 80/20 stratified train/test split (random_state=42) held out for final comparison, plus 5-fold stratified CV on the training set for a more stable estimate per model. Identical preprocessing pipeline (ColumnTransformer: median-impute+standard-scale numerics, one-hot encode categoricals with handle_unknown='ignore') applied to all model families so differences reflect the learning algorithm, not feature engineering. Four model families chosen to span distinct paradigms: Logistic Regression (linear), KNN with k=25 (instance-based), Random Forest with 300 trees (bagged trees), HistGradientBoosting (boosted trees) — all left near default hyperparameters (light tuning only, e.g. RF min_samples_leaf=2, KNN k=25) since the question concerns model family choice, not exhaustive per-model tuning. ROC-AUC chosen as primary metric because the target is imbalanced (~24% positive class) and ROC-AUC is threshold-independent; accuracy reported as a secondary/interpretability metric. 'Meaningful effect' operationalized as the spread (max-min) in test-set ROC-AUC across the four families.
